curriculum.lesson_evidence: Advertisements and posters persuade with slogans, images, layout and selective facts aimed at a target audience.
curriculum.scope_limit: Single lesson: partial evidence. Cross-check existing card mapping and NESA content point.

lesson.child_mission: Advertisements and posters persuade with slogans, images, layout and selective facts aimed at a target audience.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same strategy to an unfamiliar topic or audience, then compare the effect of two different choices.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
For a library poster with a giant book and "Read your way to adventure", name audience, slogan job and one visual choice.

FEEDBACK
Audience: students/families. Slogan: invites reading as adventure. Visual: giant book draws the eye to reading.

CHECK
Pretty design alone does not prove the offer is good; evaluate the claim.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Compare two ads or posters. Record audience, slogan, two techniques and one fact that is missing. Decide which is more trustworthy and why.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Advertisements and posters persuade with slogans, images, layout and selective facts aimed at a target audience.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Compare two ads or posters. Record audience, slogan, two techniques and one fact that is missing. Decide which is more trustworthy and why. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Audience: students/families. Slogan: invites reading as adventure. Visual: giant book draws the eye to reading. Reasoning: I used advertisement by attending to poster and explain why it matters rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Pretty design alone does not prove the offer is good; evaluate the claim. Correction: Audience: students/families. Slogan: invites reading as adventure. Visual: giant book draws the eye to reading. Why: the correction restores accurate use of advertisement.

Parent: Likely misconception: Pretty design alone does not prove the offer is good; evaluate the claim. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating advertisement on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with advertisement, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Require independently produced work with a specific supporting detail. / Require misconception + correction + purpose-linked reason..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
A sports-club poster uses bright balls, the slogan "Join the fun squad!" and a free-trial date to attract families.

Audience: students/families. Slogan: invites reading as adventure. Visual: giant book draws the eye to reading.
teach_steps.explain:
Advertisements and posters persuade with slogans, images, layout and selective facts aimed at a target audience.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
